summary.headline: Gufic Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to Rs 288.4 crore, but EBITDA margin was 17.23% amid API and freight cost pressure.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 288.4 crore versus Rs 230.4 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of Rs 49.7 crore (17.23% margin, against 16.45%). Profit after tax was Rs 23.5 crore (8.15% margin) versus Rs 14.9 crore (6.47%). Management said the Indore plant reached EBITDA breakeven, with US FDA pre-approval inspection completed (three observations, being addressed) and an EU compliance report submitted awaiting certification. Gross margin was pressured by rupee-driven API import cost increases and higher domestic and international freight, which management expects to normalise over one to two quarters. Inventory rose to around Rs 370 crore, which management expects to fall to Rs 325-330 crore by March 2027.

segments.name: Domestic formulations
segments.commentary: Management put domestic at about 48-49% of H1 revenue, growing about 12% YoY; hospital injectables carry price erosion, and 12-15% is seen as the achievable range. Stunox botulinum toxin combined business is about Rs 3.5-3.6 crore annualised, targeted to grow 25-30% a year.

segments.name: International formulations
segments.commentary: About 25-26% of H1 revenue, growing about 20-22% YoY; 65-70% of revenue comes from regulated markets. New Saudi Arabia registrations, Chile first order, and UK/Germany anti-fungal orders were reported.

segments.name: CMO/CDMO
segments.commentary: About 19-20% of H1 revenue, growing about 4-5% YoY, with Semaglutide and Astro-Mavi-Bactam contributions. Management said 22 countries' registrations for semaglutide are expected to begin contributing from Q1-Q2 FY28.

segments.name: Indore plant (injectables)
segments.commentary: Indore reached EBITDA breakeven; management expects it to cover interest and depreciation by Q4 FY27. Four production lines ran at higher output than in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Management targets 15-20% YoY revenue growth; domestic growth 12-15% is the stated achievable range.
EBITDA margin target of 22-25% in the near term, with about 1% annual improvement; management said 18.5% is achievable as international mix rises.
Gross margin pressure from API and freight costs expected to normalise over one to two quarters.

Indore: four to six molecules to be added between November 2026 and March 2027; EU entry targeted by September 2027; US supply expected within three to six months of approval, with approvals targeted around February-March 2027.
Semaglutide and international registrations: 182 MAs targeted by December 2026; peak revenue from the 824 million USD addressable market expected in three to four years.
capex_capacity: Indore plant: US FDA pre-approval inspection completed with three observations, being addressed within the stipulated timeframe; EU compliance report submitted, awaiting certification.
Depot suit ready for trials; lipid-based anti-fungal spray-dry route close to completion; injectable immersion format moved through scale-up.
Annual capex of about Rs 20-30 crore is funded from internal accruals; H1 FY27 capex on GLP-1 and depot/liposomal infrastructure was about Rs 22-25 crore.
Botulinum toxin international entry would need about USD 15-20 million (dedicated facility of USD 9-11 million plus clinical and regulatory costs); management said it is not ready to commit.
demand_pricing: Hospital injectables face annual price erosion; management cited volume growth of 30-35% translating to only 8-10% value growth in some molecules.
Raw material prices (API, certain antibiotics such as Meropenem) remain high; some prices eased from October, but management is taking it quarter by quarter.
Semaglutide: about 1.5 million USD spent this year on registrations; 22-23 countries targeted.
Dual chamber bag (DCB) products: two launched, one more expected October-December 2026, and two more targeted by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin dip in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to rupee depreciation raising API import costs, which could not be passed on immediately, plus higher domestic and international freight. EBITDA margin fell from about 18.1% to 17.23%.

qa_highlights.question: Has Indore reached EBITDA breakeven and when will it cover interest and depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Indore is already EBITDA-positive in Q2 and is expected to cover interest and depreciation by Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US FDA inspection outcome and the CDMO outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The pre-approval inspection was linked to a US partner's product; management targets four to six molecules to be added between November 2026 and March 2027, with US supply expected Q2-Q3 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital and debtor/inventory build-up rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 40-50 crore of inventory is held for US supply security and validation batches, and inventory should fall to Rs 325-330 crore by March 2027. No long-term loans were taken in the past year, with capex funded internally.

qa_highlights.question: Why was EU certification delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: A bioequivalence study had to be repeated for a modification under the new Annex 1 requirements, adding about 45 days to a roughly two-and-a-half month delay; the EU audit took place in December.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and growth of the semaglutide and botulinum toxin opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: The semaglutide addressable market is about USD 824 million across 22-24 countries, with a 10-15% share target over three to four years. Botulinum toxin is about Rs 3.5-3.6 crore annualised and is targeted to grow 25-30% a year.

risks_watch: US FDA observations at Indore must be closed on time; US supply depends on partner approvals, with timing guided to February-March 2027.
Inventory of about Rs 370 crore and receivable days (about 200 days as stated on the call) keep working capital high.
API and freight costs remain high, and management said Q3 margin is not assured to normalise.
Hospital price erosion limits domestic value growth to about 12%, below the 15-20% company target.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on regulatory progress and international registrations but cautious on timing, repeatedly qualifying US and EU revenue start dates and margin normalisation. Answers on pricing, inventory and margins were candid about pressures, while long-range targets were framed as aspirational.
key_quotes: So it's good to see approvals and orders arriving together.
There were three observations and the team is addressing them within the stipulated timeframe.
I would still take it quarter at one quarter at a time let's see what happens post Q3 Q4 and how this entire world tapers down

tone.note: Management was confident on regulatory progress, registrations and the Indore breakeven but cautious on US/EU start dates, margin normalisation and raw material costs; analysts pushed on gross margin dip, inventory and working capital build-up, and EU certification delay.
